picks.title: mattpocock/skills: Skills for Real Engineers
picks.summary: Matt Pocock's open collection of production agent skills, published straight from his .agents directory - 272k stars and #8 on GitHub trending today.
picks.implementation_idea: A junior-heavy engineering org could adopt the skill patterns as team-wide agent defaults, turning one senior's workflow into every developer's baseline.
picks.gist: A working engineer's ready-made instructions for steering coding agents, free to copy.
picks.analogy: Like peeking over a chef's shoulder at their recipe cards.
picks.why: Shows how experts guide AI programmers, openly shared this week.

picks.title: VoiceStudio: open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative with voice cloning, dubbing and dictation in 646 languages
picks.summary: VoiceStudio is an open-source, fully-local voice AI studio: voice cloning from a 3-second sample, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobook creation in 646 languages. Ships via Docker with an official Google Colab notebook for zero-install use.
picks.implementation_idea: A media or education startup can run privacy-safe voice cloning and multilingual video dubbing on its own servers, generating localized audiobooks or course narration in dozens of languages with no per-minute API cost.
picks.gist: Clone voices from a 3-second sample, then dub or dictate in 646 languages, on your own computer.
picks.analogy: Like a recording studio that runs entirely on your laptop.
picks.why: Trending #1 on GitHub with 51k stars: voice work without sending audio to a company's servers.

picks.title: Paperclip: the app people use to manage agents at work
picks.summary: Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents: org charts, budgets, governance, heartbeats and a ticket system in one dashboard.
picks.implementation_idea: A small company running several AI agents can organize them like a team, with roles, token budgets and approval gates before any agent spends money or ships changes.
picks.gist: One dashboard to give your AI agents jobs, budgets, and rules at work.
picks.analogy: Like an org chart and budget spreadsheet for robot coworkers.
picks.why: 95,874-star tool trending #1 as companies deploy multiple AI agents together.

picks.title: Pi.dev adds MCP to core: 'You Said No MCP'
picks.summary: Pi.dev reverses its public no-MCP stance, integrating Model Context Protocol into the core of its agentic coding platform with a 'Codemode' sandbox for tool composition.
picks.implementation_idea: A dev-tools team could build an MCP-gateway service exposing a company's internal APIs as Pi-compatible tools, letting small coding agents compose enterprise workflows without custom glue code.
picks.gist: Coding platform now lets AI assistants connect to outside tools and data.
picks.analogy: Like giving your assistant a master key for every office door.
picks.why: 111,268-star platform reverses stance on how AI tools connect to software.
